answer_1.quote: Our system, the Intent-Guided Assistant (IGA), combines controllable text generation with text infilling; we build an authoring assistant capable of following fine-grained user directives (e.g., add descriptive text, use idiomatic language, or paraphrase a clunky bit of wording).
answer_1.outputs: Fluent and coherent text conditioned on rhetorical directives such as cause, effect, contrast, description, biography, idiom, and paraphrase.

answer_2.quote: We compare IGA with ILM on automatic metrics such as ROUGE ... and self-BLEU ... We also compute BLEURT, BLEU, self-BLEU, and iBLEU scores.

answer_4.quote: For each output, three Mechanical Turkers are shown the gold completion as well as the generated text and asked to choose which is more fluent, coherent, and adequate at fulfilling the author intent, using a five-point scale... We also conduct a user study with twelve computer science graduate students who write short stories and provide feedback.
answer_4.guideline: Annotators compare generated text to gold completions and rate fluency, coherence, and adequacy on a five-point scale; participants in the user study provide self‑reported feedback and post‑session survey responses.
